title: Mercedes-Benz Innovation
description: Co-designed and led a full-day innovation workshop for Mercedes-Benz in Spain with Bridge education, exploring how transformative forces will reshape the customer journey by 2035. Teams used AI tools to prototype landing pages, interactive prototypes, and explainer videos within the session — the majority with no prior AI experience — and pitched results Shark Tank-style to Mercedes management.

sections.title: Context
sections.body: Mercedes-Benz commissioned a full-day innovation workshop for their leadership and product team in Spain, focused on the 2035 customer journey. The brief came through The Bridge School. The day brought together ~30 participants from across the organisation to explore how transformative forces — autonomous driving, electrification, platform models, sustainability — would reshape the way customers discover, buy, use, and end ownership of a car.

sections.title: Problem
sections.body: The automotive industry is facing simultaneous disruption across hardware, software, and services. Mercedes-Benz needed to move their team beyond incremental thinking and get concrete about what the customer journey looks like in 2035 — and what that means for the business today. The challenge was not just inspiration but actionable output: teams needed to leave with a concrete initiative they could take forward.

sections.title: My role
sections.body: I co-designed and led the full day as lead facilitator, working with sector experts in mobility, energy, and sustainability. I structured the agenda, developed the frameworks used in the workshop, ran the morning keynote session, and facilitated the afternoon design sprint and Shark Tank-style pitch session. I also developed the supporting materials including the Journey Canvas 2035 and the Horizons Framework.

sections.title: Approach
sections.body:
The day was split into two halves. The morning built a shared foundation: projecting the current Mercedes customer journey, presenting cases of industries that had reinvented theirs (Netflix, Spotify, Airbnb), then unpacking five disruptive forces through external examples — Power Shift, Code on Wheels, Beyond Ownership, Freedom on Demand, and Green Loop. A live-voting session on the 2035 customer profile closed the morning with a shared point of view.

The afternoon shifted to creation. Teams were divided across three work horizons — Car-as-a-Product, Car-as-a-Platform, and Car-as-a-Service — and worked through a structured design sprint to build a Journey Canvas 2035, then develop a single moonshot initiative. Teams pitched Shark Tank-style to a panel of Mercedes management, with live audience voting on the most audacious, most viable, and most customer-centric concepts.

A key element of the afternoon was hands-on AI prototyping. Teams used AI tools to build tangible outputs within the session: landing pages for their concepts, interactive prototypes, and short explainer videos presenting the service to the investor panel. Most participants had no prior experience with AI tools — the session was designed so that this was not a barrier, and the majority were able to produce working prototypes by the end of the day.

sections.title: Outcome
sections.body:
• 3 teams developed concrete 2035 initiatives pitched to Mercedes management
  • Each team delivered a landing page, prototype, and explainer video built with AI tools within the session
  • Large majority of participants had no prior AI experience yet produced tangible, presentable outputs on the day
